title: The Importance of Recognizing Sin
summary: This hadith emphasizes the importance of recognizing sin as a sin and condemning it as part of maintaining faith.
translation: One of the evils and trials of today's times is that people do not consider sin as sin, and the very notion of sinfulness is disappearing from their hearts. In the Holy Hadith, it is mentioned that if a person sees sin being committed and likes it, not considering it bad, then it is as if that person has committed the sin and was present there. A person who considers the sin bad is understood as if they were not present there. Therefore, in the Holy Hadith, such a person who may not be present but does not consider sin bad is considered like those present. Thus, it is clear that a person must always keep the notion of sin in mind to avoid it. If one sees someone committing a sin, they should first try to stop it with their tongue and hands; if not possible, they should consider it bad in their heart, which is a sign of faith. If it becomes less than this, meaning a person does not consider sin as sin or as wrong, then they should reflect on the level of their faith.

title: Guarding One’s Gaze in Islam
summary: The importance of controlling one's gaze as per Islamic teachings to avoid sin. Lowering the gaze is linked to purity, as instructed in the Quran, and lewd gazing is considered the 'Mother of Evils.' It is described as a poisoned arrow and is harmful, leading to inner moral corruption. A sudden glance may be forgivable, but intentional looks with lust break character and diminish spiritual delight. Muslims are advised to avoid it to maintain the sweetness of faith and worship.
translation: Looking at inappropriate things is a grave sin. The Quran specifically instructs believing men and women to restrain their gaze and protect their chastity. The verse says, "Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts; that is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do." When a person's eyes become uncontrolled, it often leads to immorality and is the root of many evils. Scholars call lewd gazing the 'Mother of Evils.' In the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), it is said that the gaze is a poisoned arrow of Iblis (Satan). A glance injects poison into the heart. The 'zina of the eyes' is to look with lust. If a person gazes at a non-mahram with lust, it is as though committing adultery in the heart. However, a sudden glance is forgivable, but intentionally and repeatedly looking with lust at a non-mahram causes significant harm and robs one of the delight of good deeds, as Satan embellishes the faces of non-mahrams. Even from a distance, everything may appear attractive. Consequently, once a seed of sin is planted in the heart, one tends to seek sinful opportunities. Imam Ghazali (may Allah have mercy on him) said a glance creates a thought, which turns into desire and leads to intention. If a Muslim sees a woman's beauty once and then lowers their gaze, Allah rewards them with the delight of worship. Another hadith states that anyone who refrains from lewd gazing for fear of Allah will receive faith that they will feel the sweetness of in their heart. This sin is prevalent, so everyone, regardless of age or gender, should strive to avoid it. It is a dangerous sin, which sometimes deprives a person of the sweetness of worship.

title: Reciting Darood on Friday Night
summary: This hadith emphasizes the importance of reciting Darood on Friday night. It mentions that reciting Darood is beneficial both in this world and the hereafter. It serves as a gratitude gesture towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and Allah and His angels also join in this act. The Prophet encouraged reciting Darood abundantly on Friday and its night, promising his intercession for those who do so. It is encouraged to aim for at least 300 times or more, involving the household to bring blessings and peace. An angel will convey the gift and names to the Prophet, bringing joy and forgiveness from Allah.
translation: Tonight is the night of Friday, and on Friday night, one should abundantly recite Darood. Besides providing worldly and afterlife benefits, it is necessary to present Darood to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a gesture of gratitude for his favors upon us. This act is such that Allah Himself joins in. All acts of worship are performed by us alone, but Allah and His angels also send blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and we are commanded to do so as well. Thus, make a special effort to recite Darood today because the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stated that the best of your days is Friday. On this day, recite Darood abundantly because your Darood is conveyed to me. Another hadith mentions that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said to recite Darood abundantly on Friday and its night; whoever does so will receive my intercession on the Day of Judgment. Therefore, recite Darood as much as possible, at least three hundred times or more, as you wish—be it one lakh, two lakh, three thousand, four thousand, or any number. Involve your household, assign them the responsibility to complete these numbers so that blessings, mercy, safety, and peace descend upon your home. Send a gift from your household to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and an angel will convey your and your household’s names, along with your parents', to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), bringing him joy from the gift sent. On this basis, may Allah forgive us all.

title: Steadfastness in Faith and Practice
summary: A discussion on the concept of steadfastness (Istiqamah) in Islam, highlighting its importance as staying firm on Allah’s path in all aspects of life. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized this by referring to a challenging verse from Surah Hud. A companion asked for a concise piece of advice, to which the Prophet replied, affirming belief in Allah and remaining steadfast. Great rewards are promised in the Quran for those who maintain this steadiness.
translation: What is steadfastness, i.e., Istiqamah? The word 'Istiqamah' is small, but its meaning holds a grand vastness. In a literal sense, it means to stand upright without leaning to any side. However, in the context of Shariah and Sunnah, it implies that a person remains straight on Allah’s path in their beliefs, dealings, acts of worship, character, social life, earning, spending, and all areas of life, adhering to the boundaries set by Allah without deviating in any aspect. It is not about performing an action against Shariah when something contrary appears but rather adhering completely to the commands of Shariah and practicing it consistently. Hence, it is narrated about the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) that no verse was revealed to him more difficult during his prophethood than the verse from Surah Hud: 'So remain on a right course as you have been commanded' (11:112). At one occasion, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Surah Hud made me old.' It refers specifically to this verse. If any advice is paramount, it is maintaining steadfastness in faith and practice until death. A companion named Sufyan Thaqafi, perhaps Sufyan bin Abdullah Thaqafi, requested a comprehensive piece of advice, upon which the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Say I have believed in Allah, then remain steadfast.' Thus, steadfastness means remaining firm, not swept away by inclinations, but maintaining faith in Allah and His Messenger. Promises of great rewards are mentioned for those who declare, 'Our Lord is Allah' and maintain this course: angels will descend upon them, saying, 'Do not fear or grieve but rejoice in Paradise that you are promised.' On this life and the Hereafter, they will be friends, and they will receive whatever they desire and ask for, enjoying the hospitality of Allah, Who is Forgiving, Merciful. This Qur’anic verse from Surah Hamim Sajda highlights the significant promises for steadfastness, showing its great importance as divine advice and urging consistent adherence to it throughout one’s life.

title: Influence of Deeds on Future Generations
summary: Good deeds, such as teaching the Quran, continue to yield rewards as others follow them. Similarly, initiating bad practices brings ongoing sin. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized the importance of starting good practices, which bring rewards to both initiators and followers. Conversely, those who start harmful practices, like the first murder by Qabil, bear the sin as others follow. It's vital to avoid starting actions against Shariah, as they can perpetuate sin. Ensuring accuracy in sharing information is crucial to prevent unintentional sin.
translation: In life, we perform many good deeds that remain even after us, and others adopt them as virtuous actions. This chain continues to be recorded in our Book of Deeds as long as the action is performed, if it is good. For example, if we taught someone the Quran or helped someone become a Hafiz, and they in turn teach others or help them become Hafiz, then as long as people continue to become Hafiz through any link in this chain, the reward will continue to reach us. But the same is true for bad deeds. If a person does wrong and others follow, that sin remains as well. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Whoever initiates a good practice in Islam, it will be rewarded, and the reward of those who follow it will not diminish." Scholars say that those who obey later still get the reward based on their righteous actions, and the one who invites to good gets rewarded for their effort. Similarly, whoever initiates wrongdoing will accrue sin as others follow, like the sin of murder is upon Qabil, the first murderer, as narrated by Abdullah bin Masud (may Allah be pleased with him) from the Prophet (peace be upon him). He said that every unjust killing brings a share of its sin to Qabil because he was the first to initiate killing. The story is also in the Quran that Qabil killed Habil. This hadith warns against starting any such work that is against Shariah because this sin keeps accumulating to the initiator. Today, we share posts without verifying or make videos viral regardless of their truth or Shariah permissibility. This could cause us sin even after we pass away. Therefore, creating good deeds is virtuous, while initiating bad deeds is dangerous and must be avoided. May Allah protect us all.

title: Two Sins Leading to Divine War
summary: The hadith discusses two grave sins that provoke Allah's wrath: engaging in usury and showing enmity towards Allah’s friends, which leads to a divine declaration of war against the perpetrator.
translation: There are two sins so dangerous that Allah has stated that if a person is involved in these sins, He declares war against them. One sin is well-known and mentioned in the Quran, which is usury. If you do not desist from dealing in usury, Allah declares war against you. The second matter is mentioned in a hadith narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) where the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, Allah said: Whoever shows enmity against a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him.' This means that if someone harms one of Allah's close friends or allies, due to the severe hatred of the act, Allah declares war against them. Or it could also mean that enmity against My friend is like enmity against Me, and if someone fights Me, I will declare war against them. Thus, it is clear that no one should show hostility towards Allah's friends, close, or righteous servants. If you cannot benefit them, at least do not harm them. May Allah protect us all.

title: The Joy of Seeking Forgiveness
summary: This hadith highlights Allah's immense joy when a person seeks forgiveness. It compares this joy to a lost person finding their camel in the wilderness. The Prophet (peace be upon him) himself sought forgiveness many times daily, emphasizing its importance. The Quran instructs believers to seek forgiveness, promising worldly and spiritual benefits. Allah is always ready to accept repentance until the sun rises from the west. The practice of frequently saying 'Astaghfirullah' is encouraged.
translation: Frequent seeking of forgiveness, asking Allah for forgiveness, and crying before Allah is immensely beloved by Him. Engaging in these acts of humility is greatly favored. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stated in a hadith that Allah feels immense happiness at the repentance of His servant, like a person who, after losing his camel in the wilderness, suddenly finds it. This is how joyful Allah becomes when a servant returns to Him, seeks forgiveness, and pleases Him. Despite being innocent, the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to seek forgiveness more than seventy times a day—some narrations say over a hundred times—to teach the Ummah. The Quran also commands, 'Seek forgiveness from your Lord and then repent to Him.' Thus, frequent seeking of forgiveness is beloved to Allah, and cannot be achieved through neglect. By repeatedly asking for forgiveness, not only are sins erased, but worldly blessings also increase, such as sustenance, offspring, and provisions. Therefore, frequent asking for forgiveness directs Allah’s attention and pleasure toward the person. The Prophet (peace be upon him) mentioned that Allah extends His hand to accept repentance every night until the sun rises from the west. If this was unimportant to Allah, He would not extend His hand every day and night, awaiting repentance. The Prophet (peace be upon him) also stated that repentance is accepted until the sun rises from the west. Anyone who repents before then will have their repentance accepted by Allah. One should frequently pray to Allah, saying 'Astaghfirullah' many times, from a minimum of 1,200 to a maximum of 12,000 times a day, or whatever feels suitable, to seek His pleasure.

title: Warnings Against Oppression and Stinginess
summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) warned against oppression as it leads to darkness on the Day of Judgment, and cautioned against stinginess, which led previous communities to destruction, bloodshed, and the violation of prohibitions.
translation: Jabir bin Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'Avoid oppression, for oppression will lead to darkness on the Day of Resurrection.' This signifies that oppressors will be engulfed in darkness, lacking the light that believers will have, as mentioned in the Quran: 'Their light will run forward before them and by their right hands.' Oppressors will be deprived of this. Some scholars interpret 'darkness' as suffering and trials endured by oppressors on that Day. The hadith also states, 'Avoid stinginess, as it destroyed those before you. It led them to shed blood and make lawful what was forbidden.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) indicated that extreme love for wealth leads to a loss of respect for others and blurs the line between lawful and unlawful, inciting violence. Allah also states, 'And the wrongdoers will have no devoted friends and no one will advocate for them.' Another hadith by Abu Huraira (may Allah be pleased with him) mentions that justice will be served on the Day of Resurrection, illustrating that even animals will receive recompense, highlighting the certainty of justice for human oppression.

title: The Duty of Enjoining Good
summary: This hadith highlights the importance of enjoining good and forbidding evil. Believers should encourage good deeds and try to prevent bad ones. If unable, they should at least disapprove of them in their hearts. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) warned that neglecting this duty could lead to divine punishment, after which prayers would not be answered.
translation: A believer should praise and encourage good deeds and offer help. They should stop bad deeds to the best of their ability. If unable to do so, they should at least despise them in their heart. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or Allah will send His punishment upon you. Then you will call upon Him, but He will not respond to you." (Narrated by Tirmidhi). The hadith emphasizes that performing the duty of enjoining good and forbidding evil brings Allah's mercy and acceptance of prayers. Neglect leads to divine punishment that prayers cannot avert. Another hadith supports this, stating that failure to perform this duty will result in evil people being empowered over you, and even the prayers of the righteous will not be accepted until this duty is resumed.

title: Hasten in Doing Good Deeds
summary: The Prophet Muhammad advised that one should act immediately on thoughts of doing good, as trials will arise, making it difficult to maintain faith.
translation: Sometimes, thoughts of doing good deeds arise in the heart. One should not delay; as soon as such intentions form, the deed should be done immediately. For example, if you feel like giving charity while going somewhere, do it at once. Similarly, if you feel like praying two rak'ahs or reciting the Qur'an, do it without delay. The world often keeps a person occupied, and without knowing, time passes. Therefore, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) instructed, 'Hasten to do good deeds before trials arrive like pieces of a dark night. A person will wake up as a believer and become a disbeliever by evening, or be a believer in the evening and a disbeliever by morning as he sells his religion for worldly goods.' This narration by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) is found in Sahih Muslim, where the Prophet emphasized that one must hasten to perform good deeds because severe trials will come, each worse than the previous, like the increasing darkness of night. In such times, opportunities might not come, and the ultimate test will be when a person shifts from belief to disbelief due to worldly temptations, thus trading their faith just for worldly gain.

title: Best Time to Give Charity
summary: The most rewarding charity is given when you are healthy, fearing poverty, and hoping for wealth, and not delaying until the time of death, as the wealth then belongs to heirs.
translation: In a hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) described the charity that carries the greatest reward. Narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), a man asked the Prophet (peace be upon him), 'O Messenger of Allah, which charity carries the most reward?' The Prophet (peace be upon him) replied, 'Giving charity when you are healthy, hesitant, fearing poverty, and hoping for wealth.' He further advised not to delay charity until death approaches, when a person might start assigning belongings, as by then, they belong to the heirs. According to Islamic law, inheritance is mainly for the heirs, with up to one-third for bequests; debts are settled first after one's passing.

title: Love for Others What You Love for Yourself
summary: This hadith emphasizes that true faith involves loving for others what you love for yourself. It highlights both worldly and spiritual goods, encouraging believers to wish well for their fellow Muslims.
translation: Each of us desires the best for ourselves, quality items, comfort, and convenience. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that a person cannot be a true believer until they love for their brother what they love for themselves. In a narration by Al-Nasa'i, it is mentioned: 'By Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself of good.' This includes both worldly and spiritual goodness. Worldly goodness involves honor, a prosperous life, wealth, good family, and obedient children. Spiritual goodness involves performing righteous deeds, ending life with faith, being saved from the grave's hardships, and the Day of Judgment's difficulties, as well as the torment of Hell, and attaining Paradise and the sight of Allah. A person should desire the same for all their Muslim brothers, which is a sign of faith. Furthermore, just as one should love good things for others, one should also dislike for them what they dislike for themselves. This applies both to what one loves and what one does not love.

title: Human Dependence on Divine Help
summary: The essence of human existence is their inherent dependence on Allah. Despite attempts to achieve goals through personal effort, it is ultimately Allah who fulfills needs. Like a compassionate father helping his child reach their destination, Allah responds to the sincere prayers and petitions of His servants, granting them assistance and mercy.
translation: A human being's nature is that they are essentially in need. In any situation, they lack the power to accomplish anything on their own. The reality is that when a person turns to Allah, asks from Him, and pleads with Him, Allah arranges all matters for them. Therefore, the essence of a human is that they are inherently in need. It is merely their delusion to think they can achieve their goals through their own planning and reach their destination. The truth is, Allah Almighty is the true doer, and all human efforts are merely a means to attract Allah's mercy. Just like a compassionate father feels for his small child who attempts to walk, seeing them fall repeatedly, knowing they cannot reach their goal through their own strength, he eventually extends his finger to help them reach their destination. Similarly, our beloved Sustainer shows mercy and helps us reach our goals that we cannot reach on our own. If the child acknowledges their helplessness, sheds tears, and looks towards their father while calling in a trembling voice, the father's heart fills with love, and he immediately picks up the child. This is also true of our Merciful, Generous Sustainer, who, hearing the cries, pleas, and prayers from the hearts of His servants, promptly pays attention, and His divine mercy fulfills our desires. Allah, in the Holy Quran, commands His servants, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Therefore, one should strive with eagerness and devotion, and plead with Allah to achieve all their desires. This is the only path where a person can prove themselves entirely devoid of any means, reminding themselves that whatever they have is only from Allah. 'O Allah, make this work possible for me, achieve this for me, and grant me favor as You have always favored me.' Therefore, there should be an atmosphere of prayer at home with children, with wives, with relatives, gathering everyone for collective prayers with eagerness, passion, and regularity.

title: Living a Dignified Life of Obedience
summary: A dignified life is achieved by spending one's time in obedience to Allah. When a person aligns their life with God's law, their deeds and time gain eternal value. Even if they leave this world, they receive everlasting rewards in the afterlife for their good deeds. Thus, life should not mimic random behaviors but be shaped by Islamic principles. Islam offers complete guidance for a dignified, peaceful life. The Hadith mentions that righteous people leave the world successively, and those who do not contribute meaningfully remain like chaff. Therefore, one must strive to live a life esteemed by Allah, following Shariah and making time valuable.
translation: A person should live their worldly life in a dignified manner. When will a dignified life be lived? When a person spends their time and life moments in obedience to Allah. When one conforms their time to God's law and obedience, the benefit will be that this act and time will become everlasting. The reason is that although one may not remain in this world, the reward in the afterlife for these good deeds will be eternal. It is understood that if one makes their time useful by living in obedience to Allah in this world, then a priceless, eternal life will be their destiny. Therefore, time should be made useful, and life should be lived in a dignified manner. It is not about living by imitating any random person's behavior or character. Instead, Islam is entirely civil and peaceful. Every wish can be fulfilled and every lesson learned from it. There is no aspect of life that is not found here, and no instructions unavailable. Therefore, we should strive to shape our lives according to Islam in every matter. May Allah make us all live dignified lives. The Prophet's (SAW) Hadith states that the righteous people will gradually leave the world, and those who are useless will not be of any concern to Allah, remaining like chaff in the world. It shows that Allah values righteous people, so He calls them soon. Bad people are not valued by Allah, so they remain. Hence, we must live life as good people, esteemed by Allah, and live shaping ourselves according to Shariah and by making our time useful.
reviewIssues: Retitled for clarity

title: Angels' Prayers for the Generous
summary: The hadith emphasizes the importance of generosity in Islam. It explains that two angels pray every morning; one for the generous, that they receive more wealth and rewards, and another against the miserly, asking for the destruction of their wealth due to their stinginess. Muslims are encouraged to give according to their means, as Allah favors those who help the needy.
translation:
Allah Almighty has always encouraged spending, giving in His path, helping the poor, and supporting orphans. Some commands hold the status of obligation, some are compulsory, and others are voluntary. Thus, those with wealth upon whom zakat is obligatory will be sinful if they do not pay it. Similarly, the charity before the Eid prayer is obligatory; failing to give it will incur sin. Additionally, voluntary alms can be given according to one's financial capability—assign a fixed amount from your profit, like a small percentage, and partner with Allah in charity. Whenever leaving home, gather donations in a box, and once accumulated, fulfill a significant need for someone poor. Allah loves such servants greatly.

In Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that every morning, two angels descend. One prays for the generous, that Allah grants them more wealth abundantly as a reward for their spending, and that Allah rewards them manifold in the hereafter. Conversely, the other angel curses the miser who hoards and spends unwisely, asking Allah to destroy their wealth for spending in places of Allah’s displeasure. The angels are highly regarded and obedient to Allah, so consider how accepted their prayers would be—one for the generous and another against the miserly. Therefore, regardless of how little you have, develop the habit of giving. Allah loves givers, not takers. The Quran expresses this with words like 'spend, spend.' Live well, earn well, and facilitate the poor’s livelihood through sacrifices and charities like zakat, donations, and gifts.

Hence, act on Allah's command and join in the prayers of the angels while avoiding their curses. May Allah make us among those whose deeds weigh heavily on the scales of deeds, who receive their record in the right hand. Pray that Allah counts us among His most accepted servants.

title: Rewards of Quran Recitation and Helping Others
summary: This Hadith from Sahih Muslim, narrated by Abu Hurairah, highlights the spiritual benefits of Quran recitation and aiding others. Reciting the Quran brings tranquility and mercy, with angels surrounding the reciter's home. It emphasizes helping others by relieving a believer's distress and easing a debtor's burden, which leads to divine assistance and reward in this world and the hereafter. The Hadith also stresses that personal actions, rather than lineage, determine one's success.
translation:
Reciting the Quran is indeed a virtuous act that brings great benefits and goodness. While it brings rewards in the hereafter, one worldly benefit is that the angels surround the reciter's home, tranquility descends upon it, and divine mercy covers it, and Allah mentions them among the angels close to Him. This is narrated in Sahih Muslim from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) where the Prophet (peace be upon him) shared important guidance.

One teaching is that whoever alleviates a believer's worldly distress, Allah will alleviate their distress on the Day of Judgment. Whoever eases the burden of a debtor will find that Allah eases burdens for them in this world and in the hereafter, and whoever conceals another’s faults, Allah will conceal their faults in this world and the hereafter. Allah is in the aid of His servant as long as the servant aids their brother.

Additionally, whoever takes a path seeking knowledge of the Quran, Allah makes their path to Paradise easy. Those who gather in Allah's houses to recite and study His Book are enveloped in tranquility, covered in mercy, surrounded by angels, and Allah speaks of them to those close to Him. Furthermore, it states that if one’s deeds slow them down, their lineage will not speed them up, emphasizing that success is based on personal actions, not one's lineage or status.

title: Every Good Deed is Charity
summary: The hadith emphasizes that charity is not limited to giving money but includes all good deeds, such as speaking kindly, smiling, helping, or providing good advice. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stated that every good act is considered charity. These actions fulfill human needs and earn rewards from Allah, similar to monetary charity.
translation: When the word charity is mentioned, people often think it means giving money for the sake of Allah. However, this is not entirely true; every good deed is considered charity, whether it's saying something nice or doing a good act for someone. This is what the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'Every good act is charity.' In this narration from Sahih Bukhari, the noble statement of the Prophet (peace be upon him) highlights that any act recognized as good in both Islamic law and reason is considered charity. Therefore, if someone cannot give money or thinks it is necessary to only give money, they should understand that every good deed or kind word is considered charity and earns divine reward just like giving money. Acts such as speaking kindly, smiling, helping in a beneficial act, guiding someone to goodness, giving good advice, or having a sincere intention for someone's welfare are all included. These deeds fulfill human needs and earn rewards from Allah as forms of charity. Thus, one should approach all matters with a broad understanding of charity and choose positive actions, hoping for reward.

title: The Virtue of Lending Milk-Goats
summary: This hadith discusses the virtues of lending a milk-giving goat for charity. It states that performing such good deeds with sincerity and hope for Allah's reward leads to Paradise. The hadith mentions that forty good qualities, including acts like aiding others and providing guidance, are highly valued.
translation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) enumerated many virtues of giving in charity and as gifts. In a specific hadith, he mentioned that giving a milk-giving goat as a gift is a highly esteemed quality and that whoever gifts it hoping for reward from Allah and believing in His promise will be admitted to Paradise. The Prophet stated that there are forty qualities, and the best among them is to lend a milk-giving goat for use. Anyone who practices any of these forty qualities seeking reward and believing in Allah's promise will enter Paradise. Various qualities compiled by scholars include helping in tasks, repairing sandals, concealing the faults of Muslims, sharing in their happiness, providing space in gatherings, guiding rightly, planting trees, giving good counsel, showing mercy, responding to greetings and sneezes, and removing harmful objects from paths. Particularly, lending a milk-giving goat during necessity to be returned after use is highly rewarded. This emphasizes immediate benefits, like fresh milk, showing the value in gifting such an animal.

title: Consequence of Unjust Land Seizure
summary: The hadiths warn that unjustly taking land leads to severe punishment on the Day of Judgment. The person will face carrying the soil or a collar made from seven earths as a burden.
translation: From a Hadith, as narrated by Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (may Allah be pleased with her), the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever unjustly takes even a span of land will have a collar from seven earths placed upon him on the Day of Judgment." In another Hadith, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, reportedly stated that whoever unjustly takes land or seizes it will be forced on the Day of Resurrection to carry the soil of that land on their head.

title: Importance of Cleanliness and Removing Harm
summary: Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized the importance of removing harmful objects from paths as a good deed rewarded by Allah. He also highlighted the seriousness of maintaining cleanliness in mosques, cautioning against spitting or discarding impurities there.
translation: Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that the good and bad deeds of my community were presented to me. Among the good deeds, he found that removing harmful things from the path is considered a good deed, rewarded greatly by Allah. Among the bad deeds, he found that throwing nasal discharge or spitting in the mosque is bad. Such acts often occur out of forgetfulness, but people should avoid polluting the mosque, which must be kept clean not only outwardly but also free from actions one wouldn’t do at home.

title: Value of Small Acts in Islam
summary: The hadith emphasizes that no good deed, no matter how small, should be underestimated. Even actions like smiling at others are considered praiseworthy and rewarded by Allah.
translation: No matter if the act is small or large, it is not necessary to perform great deeds for them to be accepted. Small good deeds are continuously accepted by Allah. They add significant weight to our record of deeds. Therefore, several hadiths list small actions as good deeds. If someone says 'SubhanAllah' or 'Allahu Akbar' even once, it is considered charity and a good deed. Just as one gains reward by giving charity with wealth, uttering these words also carries the reward of charity. A hadith narrated by Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) states that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) advised not to underestimate any good action, even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face. Shaykh Idris Kandhlawi (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned that meeting someone with a smile brings happiness and fosters love among people, which is commendable. It is advised to meet even those you dislike with kindness and a cheerful demeanor, as it instills respect and happiness.

title: The Importance of Small Good Deeds
summary: This hadith emphasizes that small good deeds are valuable and not to be belittled. Performing minor acts like smiling at others is rewarded as charity. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) taught that even small gestures, such as greeting people with a cheerful face, can have significant spiritual rewards. Not underestimating any good deed, no matter how small, is encouraged as it could be accepted by Allah and increase the weight of one's record of deeds.
translation: Whether small or large, it is not necessary to perform a grand deed for it to be considered good. Even minor good deeds are accepted by Allah and add weight to our record of deeds. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) highlighted in various hadiths that small acts are also virtuous. For instance, saying 'Subhan Allah' or 'Allahu Akbar' even once is considered charity and is a form of good deed. Just like giving money in charity brings rewards, uttering these words also earns the reward of charity. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, as narrated in Sahih Muslim by Hazrat Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), 'Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.' This means that even simply smiling when meeting someone brings reward. Therefore, no good deed should be seen as insignificant. This hadith stresses the importance of performing any good deed, no matter how small, as it could be accepted by Allah. Maulana Idrees Sahib Kandhalvi (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned that meeting others with a smiling face is a good deed because it brings joy and happiness, fostering love, which is a beloved action. Some scholars say one should meet even an enemy with a cheerful demeanor. There is a narration where Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was previously speaking negatively about someone. When that person arrived, the Prophet warmly greeted him. This demonstrates the importance of meeting everyone, even adversaries, with a smile, as it earns respect and brings happiness.

title: Traits of a Hypocrite
summary: The hadith describes three signs of a hypocrite: lying when speaking, breaking promises, and betraying entrusted items. Even if someone fulfills religious obligations like prayer and fasting, possessing these traits still deems them a hypocrite. Muslims must strive to avoid these characteristics and pray for their removal if present.
translation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'There are three signs of a hypocrite: when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and when entrusted, he betrays it.' Another narration adds that even if he fasts, prays, and considers himself a Muslim, but possesses these three traits, he is deemed a hypocrite. Therefore, we must pray that Allah does not instill these traits in us, and if present, we must strive to remove them.

title: Beware of Worldly Temptations and Women
summary: The Prophet ﷺ advised caution against the temptations of the world and the allure of women, noting their historical impact on the faith of past communities.
translation: Narrated Abu Saeed Al-Khudri رضي الله عنه: The Prophet ﷺ said, 'Indeed, the world is sweet and green, and Allah has appointed you as successors in it, to see how you act. So beware of the world and beware of women, for the first trial for the children of Israel was due to women.' This hadith explains that the world, like something sweet and luscious, can lose its freshness. The allure of women is emphasized as a potential cause of spiritual downfall, as seen in historical examples like Balaam bin Baura, who was led astray due to his wife's influence. Therefore, one should focus on everlasting virtues and love for Allah.
reviewIssues: Original translation included an unwarranted example of Balaam bin Ba'ura.

title: Divine Prohibition of Injustice
summary: This Hadith Qudsi highlights Allah's prohibition of injustice among His servants and His divine provision for guidance, sustenance, and forgiveness. Allah reassures that human actions neither benefit nor harm Him, and His kingdom remains unaffected by the righteousness or wickedness of His creation.
translation: Hadith narrated by Abu Dhar Al-Ghifari (may Allah be pleased with him) from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), stating that Allah Almighty said: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and for you all, so do not oppress one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I guide, so seek guidance from Me and I shall guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so seek food from Me and I shall feed you. O My servants, all of you are unclothed except those whom I clothe, so seek clothing from Me and I shall clothe you. O My servants, you sin by day and night, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I shall forgive you. O My servants, you will not be able to harm Me or benefit Me. O My servants, if your first and last, and human and jinn, were as pious as the most pious heart among you, it would not increase My kingdom in anything. O My servants, if your first and last, and human and jinn, were as wicked as the most wicked heart among you, it would not decrease My kingdom in anything. O My servants, if your first and last, and human and jinn, were to stand in one field and ask of Me, and I were to give every one whatever he asked for, that would not decrease what I have any more than a needle decreases the sea if put into it. O My servants, indeed it is but your deeds that I account for you and then recompense you for, so whoever finds good, let him praise Allah. And whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself."

title: Three Essential Advices for Believers
summary: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) gives three advices: Fear Allah always, follow a bad deed with a good one to erase it, and treat others with good character. These teachings help in achieving success in life. Maintaining piety, performing good deeds after mistakes, and having good character are emphasized as vital aspects in Islam, and on Judgment Day, good character will weigh heavily on the scales.
translation: In this hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) gives three advices. The first, narrated by Hazrat Mu'adh and Hazrat Abu Dharr (RA), is "Fear Allah wherever you are." The second is "Follow up a bad deed with a good one, for it will erase it." The third advice is "Treat people with good character." These three pieces of advice are essential for a successful life. The first is to maintain consciousness of Allah, both outwardly and inwardly, as also advised to Hazrat Abu Dharr (RA) with the words "I advise you to adopt piety in both your private and public life." The words are concise yet comprehensive, including avoiding prohibited matters according to Shariah. The second advice derives from the Quranic verse that states good deeds remove bad deeds, with scholars interpreting it to refer to all types of good deeds removing minor sins if one is regretful and determined not to repeat them. Without repentance, sins remain. The third significant point emphasizes excellent manners towards others, with several hadiths highlighting that the best among people are those with the best character. On the Day of Judgment, the heaviest deeds in a believer’s scale will be good character.
reviewIssues: Minor grammatical corrections to enhance clarity.

title: Prophetic Guidance on Trust in Allah
summary: Prophet Muhammad advised Abdullah ibn Abbas on the importance of relying on Allah, preserving His commands, and understanding that what is decreed by Allah will inevitably occur.
translation: Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated that one day I was riding behind the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'O young boy, I shall teach you some words: Guard the commandments of Allah, and He will guard you. Preserve His rights, and you will find Him before you. If you ask, ask from Allah; if you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the entire world gathers to benefit you, they cannot benefit except what Allah has decreed for you, and if they gather to harm you, they cannot harm except what Allah has written for you. The pens have been lifted, and the pages have dried.' In some versions, beyond Tirmidhi, it is noted: 'Preserve Allah's commands in prosperity, He will preserve you in adversity. Know that what missed you was never meant to reach you, and what afflicted you was never meant to pass you. Be aware that patience is the key with which Allah's help comes, and ease follows hardship.' The hadith emphasizes keeping focus on Allah for His support in all matters, with a reminder from the Quran: 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Shaykh Abdul Qadir Jilani advises adherence to this guidance for divine mercy and elevation in both worlds.

title: The Perception of Sins in Islam
summary: The hadith discusses how believers perceive sins as grave and fear them, likening sins to mountains looming over them, while non-believers dismiss them like a fly. Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that during the Prophet’s time, actions considered trivial by people today were deemed destructive sins. This illustrates that the fear of Allah influences one's caution towards sins, which diminishes as the Prophetic era becomes distant.
translation: A hadith emphasizes the seriousness and weight of sins. It describes that a believer sees sins as if they are a mountain about to fall on them, whereas a non-believer considers them as insignificant as a fly on their nose, which they easily dismiss. In this hadith, narrated by Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), he stated that people commit deeds which they view as trivial, lighter than a hair, whereas during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him), we used to consider those acts as destructive. This shows that fear of Allah leads to a fear of sins, and as the fear diminishes, a person becomes bolder in committing them. Companions of the Prophet had intense fear of Allah, making them cautious of even the smallest sin. Furthermore, the closer they were to the Prophet, the higher their level of fear and caution. However, as the era of the Prophet becomes more distant, this state is fading away, which is why Anas indicated that sins considered destructive in their time are viewed as insignificant now. This implies that cultivating fear of Allah in one's heart is crucial as it leads to distancing oneself from sins.

title: Reflecting on Time: Islamic Guidance
summary: The discussion highlights the importance of avoiding non-Islamic customs such as New Year celebrations, which include gatherings and greetings like 'Happy New Year.' It emphasizes the value of using time wisely by engaging in good deeds and remembering the finite nature of life. The teaching cautions against imitating non-Muslim practices and encourages reflection and planning for future success in life and the hereafter.
translation: Today marks the end of our current year, and tomorrow will begin the new year. In this context, it is important to recognize that eagerly waiting for midnight and congratulating each other, cutting cakes, or holding gatherings is not appropriate according to Islamic teachings, as these are practices of non-Muslims. Muslims should adhere to their traditions and follow their religious teachings. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, 'Whoever imitates a people, he becomes one of them, and their fate will be similar.' Therefore, one should avoid such gatherings and instead pray to Allah. This is a time for reflection: as part of our life ends and another begins, reminding us that life is fleeting. When we study the books of our predecessors, we learn that they made conscious efforts to perform good deeds every day. If they missed a day, they regretted it. Abdullah ibn Masud (may Allah be pleased with him) said he regretted nothing more than a day where the sun set without increasing his good deeds. Similarly, Hassan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) stated, 'O son of Adam, you are but a collection of days; when a day passes, so does a part of you.' When we lose our belongings, we become happy or sad; here, we lose parts of our life, yet we rejoice. Our death is approaching, our days and hours are decreasing. Hazrat Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said, 'These days are the scrolls of your life; fill them with good deeds.' If one does good deeds, that day will remain beneficial for his life and the hereafter, but if he does evil, the day will be considered wasted, and it will lead to punishment. The best way is for a person to show the virtue of Islam by avoiding meaningless activities: 'One of the beautiful traits of Islam is that a person avoids what does not concern them.' Celebrating with New Year’s parades and greetings or saying phrases like 'Happy New Year' is not appropriate according to Shariah. One should reflect on past time and prepare a plan for future success in both life and the hereafter.
reviewIssues: Title was not reflective of core message.
Summary needed adjustment for clarity.

title: Trusting in Allah for Sustenance
summary: The hadith emphasizes relying on Allah for provision, highlighting the example of birds that venture out hungry and return satiated.
translation: Allah Almighty bestows abundance upon those who truly rely on Him. This trust needs to be learned by being with elders and reading stories of the companions. In a hadith, Umar radiAllahu ta'ala 'anhu says he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'If you were to rely upon Allah with proper reliance, He would provide for you just as He provides for the birds. They go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening.'
reviewIssues: Minor wording issues corrected.

title: Daily Acts of Charity
summary: The hadith emphasizes that each joint in the human body requires an act of charity daily. This charity extends beyond monetary giving to include fair judgement, helping others with transportation, speaking kindly, walking to prayer, and removing harmful objects from pathways.
translation: Narrated from Abu Huraira, and this is an agreed-upon hadith as both Bukhari and Muslim have narrated it, that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'Each joint of a person must give charity each day the sun rises. To judge fairly between two people is charity. To assist a person with their mount, lifting them onto it or hoisting their belongings onto it, is charity. A good word is charity. Every step taken towards prayer is charity. And removing a harmful object from the road is charity.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) explains that for each joint in the human body, a person should perform charity each day. This does not necessarily mean giving money. Instead, fair judgement, aiding someone with transportation, saying a kind word, walking to prayer, and clearing the path are all acts of charity.

title: Permitted Lies for Reconciliation
summary: Certain lies are permissible to maintain peace, during war, and in marital conversations.
translation: Umm Kulthum bint Uqba bin Abi Mu'it (RA) narrated: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: ‘The person who lies to reconcile between people or to convey good or say good things is not considered a liar.’ In a narration in Sahih Muslim, there is an addition: ‘I never heard him permit any falsehood except in three cases: in war, to reconcile among people, and a man's conversation with his wife and a woman's conversation with her husband. Imam Tabari (may Allah have mercy on him) explained that in such cases, actual lying is not permissible, but rather it is about using ambiguous statements. For example, when Abu Bakr (RA) was migrating from Makkah to Madinah and someone asked him about the identity of the Prophet (peace be upon him) who was with him, Abu Bakr said, ‘He is guiding me on the way.’ The person thought it meant guiding on the physical journey, whereas Abu Bakr meant guiding to the path of Jannah. Hence, such statements are allowed for goodness, provided there is no intention of causing discord.

title: Inner Qualities Over Appearances
summary: True value in Islam is determined by one's inner qualities, such as good deeds, piety, and sincerity, rather than physical appearance or strength. On the Day of Judgment, a person with righteous actions will have worth in Allah's sight, unlike someone who relies solely on their physical presence.
translation: A person should never think that having a large, imposing, powerful body, or looking beautiful grants them true value. In worldly terms, this may bring recognition, but in the hereafter, only good character, piety, good dealings, and righteous actions will matter. As the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) made clear in a Hadith narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), a well-built person will hold no more weight than a mosquito's wing on the Day of Judgment. The Quran similarly states, 'We will not establish any weight for them on the Day of Resurrection.' This Hadith reveals that Allah values internal qualities such as deeds, faith, piety, and sincerity, not external appearance. Thus, believers are encouraged to strengthen their faith to attain real worth in Allah's view.

title: Supporting Orphans in Islam
summary: The hadith emphasizes the great reward for caring for orphans, stating that those who do so will be close to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in Paradise, comparable to the closeness of two fingers.
translation: In the society we live in, it's our responsibility to support the poor, orphans, and helpless individuals. If everyone takes this responsibility seriously and works towards it, no community will have needy people who must ask others for their needs. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) promised a great reward for caring for the helpless and orphans. In a hadith narrated by Hazrat Sahl ibn Sa'd (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'I and the one who takes care of an orphan will be in Paradise like this,' showing the gap between his index and middle fingers. He then joined them, indicating that the caretaker of an orphan will be close to him in Paradise as these fingers are close. Some hadith scholars note that the small gap signifies that such a generous person is close to the rank of prophethood, and generosity is very beloved to Allah. Thus, taking care of orphans and supporting them is a commendable act that should be practiced.
reviewIssues: Minor differences in wording.

title: Caring for Orphans and Its Reward
summary: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) highlighted the importance of caring for orphans, promising that those who do so will be close to him in Paradise, as illustrated by the gesture of joining two fingers.
translation: In the society we live in, it is our duty to take care of the poor, orphans, and helpless people. If every person recognizes and fulfills this duty, no community or neighborhood will have individuals needing to ask others for help. This is why the Messenger of Allah, the Holy Prophet (PBUH), gave great glad tidings for supporting the helpless and caring for orphans. There is a hadith from Hazrat Sahl bin Sa'ad (RA) in which the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said, 'I and the person who takes care of an orphan will be in Paradise like this.' And he (PBUH) showed the closeness by joining his index and middle fingers. This indicates the closeness between me and the one who supports the orphan in Paradise. Some scholars mention that the slight distance shown between the fingers indicates that the rank of prophethood is near to the generous one, and that a generous person is very beloved to Allah. Thus, it is understood that caring for orphans and organizing their support is a great act that should be pursued.

title: Supporting Widows is Greatly Rewarded
summary: Helping a widow and arranging her sustenance is said to be awarded as much as one who fights in Allah's path. It is likened to the reward of a person who constantly prays at night and fasts during the day. This hadith is agreed upon as it is in both Bukhari and Muslim.
translation: Narrated by Abu Huraira (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) conveyed that taking care of a widow's needs grants a reward like that of a person who fights in the path of Allah. It is said to be equivalent to someone who prays Tahajjud at night and consistently fasts during the day. There is some uncertainty about whether these exact words are from the Prophet (peace be upon him) or the narrator’s expression. However, if a companion relayed it, then it's considered the Prophet’s statement. This hadith is agreed upon (Muttafaqun 'alayh) in Bukhari and Muslim, indicating its high authenticity and stressing the importance of supporting a widow.
uncertaintyNote: Narrator's uncertainty if it was directly the Prophet's words.

title: Inclusivity in Wedding Invitations
summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized the importance of inclusivity in banquets, specifically wedding feasts, by criticizing those who invite only the wealthy and exclude the poor. Accepting an invitation is generally considered a religious duty, but exceptions are noted if the banquet involves un-Islamic practices.
translation: Regarding wedding feasts (walima), the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) expressed a concern narrated by Abu Huraira (may Allah be pleased with him): 'The worst food is the food of a banquet where those invited refuse, and those not invited are brought in. Whoever does not attend the invitation has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger.' Another narration from Bukhari and Muslim by Abu Huraira states: 'The food of a banquet is bad when only the rich are invited and the poor are left out.' The hadith implies that rejecting an invitation without a valid reason is disobedience to Allah and His Messenger. If a banquet involves un-Islamic practices, then refusal with a valid reason is justified. Some scholars view attending a banquet as recommended, not obligatory unless a valid excuse exists.

title: Allah's Mercy Overcomes His Wrath
summary: The hadith emphasizes that a Muslim should never lose hope in Allah's mercy, which surpasses His anger. Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) explained that Allah has a book above His Throne stating, 'My mercy prevails over My wrath.' Additionally, Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts, keeping ninety-nine for Himself and sending one to Earth. From this, all creatures show mercy to one another.
translation: A characteristic of a Muslim is that they never lose hope in God's mercy and always rely on Allah's mercy. It is Allah's mercy that gives strength in every hardship and brings relief during trials. This hope and resilience should be maintained by a Muslim, about which the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said in a Hadith that Allah's mercy precedes His wrath. According to a Hadith narrated by Hazrat Abu Huraira (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "When Allah created the creation, He wrote in a book which is with Him above the Throne: 'My mercy overcomes My anger.' In another narration, 'My mercy prevails over My wrath.' And in another narration, 'My mercy precedes My anger.' So the purpose of these narrations is that Allah's mercy is vast and encompassing over everything. In one narration, it is even mentioned that Allah made mercy into one hundred parts, retaining ninety-nine with Himself and sent one part to the earth. It is from that one part that all creatures show mercy to each other, even a beast lifts its hoof from its young fearing it might harm it. Therefore, one should always depend on Allah and, after doing all they can, place hope and trust in Allah, believing that Allah will surely fulfill their needs."

title: The Virtue of Reciting Durood on Fridays
summary: The hadith emphasizes the virtue of reciting Durood Shareef, especially on Fridays, as it is conveyed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is recommended to increase this practice on Fridays and Friday nights for the Prophet's intercession on the Day of Judgment. Durood-e-Ibrahimi is highlighted as the best form of Durood to recite in prayers.
translation: Reciting Durood Shareef is a highly esteemed practice and greatly beloved by Allah. It is pure and mandatory upon us due to the favors of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that we continually send Durood upon him, especially on Fridays. The Prophet (peace be upon him) indicated that among your days, Friday is the most virtuous, so increase the recitation of Durood on that day as it is conveyed to me. This is narrated in Musnad Ahmad, Abu Dawood, and Ibn Majah. Additionally, the Prophet (peace be upon him) stated that reciting Durood in abundance on Friday and its night will grant my intercession on the Day of Judgment. The specific Durood known as Durood-e-Ibrahimi is the best Durood, recited in prayer. If there were a better Durood in the sight of Allah or the Prophet (peace be upon him), it would have been recommended, but this Durood is strong, commendable, and contains unique qualities. Therefore, we should frequently recite this Durood to gain its blessings both inside and outside of prayer.

title: Repentance and Allah’s Forgiveness
summary: This hadith emphasizes that making a mistake is not the problem, but persisting in sin is. Humans should show humility and seek Allah's forgiveness. If they did not sin, Allah would create beings who would sin and seek forgiveness, displaying His attribute of being forgiving.
translation: If by mistake a sin is committed, it is not bad, but persisting in sin and remaining committed to it is very bad for a person. It is not fitting for a person, being a creation of Allah, to do something that shows audacity or defiance towards others. Instead, one should always be characterized by humility and bow before Allah, as Allah is most forgiving. Allah created his forgiving nature to show mercy and forgive the sins of His servants. A narration from Abu Ayyub Khalid bin Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him, quotes the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: 'If you did not sin, Allah would create people who would sin and seek forgiveness, and He would forgive them.' Allah has many attributes, including being forgiving and concealing faults. Human beings were created with both good and evil tendencies so that if evil overcomes good, they turn to Allah, who then manifests His forgiveness and mercy, leading to the pardon of sins. Ideally, humans should strive to suppress evil and enhance goodness, sin less, and seek forgiveness if they sin. They should strive to increase virtue and, if needed, make efforts to do so. If sins occur, they should quickly turn to Allah, try to extract themselves from the mire of sins, and aspire to be among the righteous. By doing so, Allah will guide them to a state where they are inclined towards goodness and stay away from sin. Persistence in seeking forgiveness and consciousness of Allah will protect against sin, as one's heart becomes sincere and steadfast. May Allah bestow upon us correct understanding and the zeal to seek His closeness and forgiveness for our sins.

title: True Kinship: Maintaining Ties Despite Severance
summary: This Hadith teaches that true kinship is not about reciprocating kindness but maintaining relations even when others sever ties.
translation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, he stated that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: 'The one who reciprocates kindness for kindness is not truly maintaining kinship. Rather, the real maintainer of kinship is the one who, when ties are severed with them, still seeks to mend them.' It is clear that if someone treats you well and you treat them well in return, that is not true kinship; it is mere reciprocation. True kinship is when, despite neglect or severed relations by others, you continue to treat them well and maintain good relations. Hence, it is reported that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, mentioned to people, 'Shall I not tell you of the best manners of this world and the hereafter?' The companions replied affirmatively. He then advised: 'Forgive those who wrong you, give to those who withhold from you, and maintain ties with those who sever them with you.'

title: Maintaining Ties of Kinship
summary: The hadith emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah, avoiding idolatry, performing prayers, giving zakat, and maintaining kinship ties. These actions are described as pathways to entering paradise and protection from hellfire. A companion of the Prophet (PBUH) sought guidance on deeds that secure paradise and prevent hellfire, to which the Prophet provided these five key practices.
translation: The blessed hadiths have greatly emphasized maintaining ties of kinship. Fulfilling the rights of blood relatives is an important duty in Islam and a significant human responsibility. If everyone attends to their relatives, no one would need to go outside their family. A man asked the Prophet (PBUH), "O Messenger of Allah, tell me a deed that will admit me to paradise and keep me away from hell." The Prophet (PBUH) said: "Worship Allah — do not worship anyone else. Do not associate partners with Him. Establish prayer, especially adhere to obligatory prayers. Pay zakat — it is obligatory on the wealthy, and not paying it keeps this responsibility unfulfilled. Maintain kinship ties." Faqih Abu Allah mentioned that five continuous deeds bring immense reward and provision from Allah: giving charity, maintaining kinship, striving in the path of Allah, remaining in a state of ablution, and obeying parents.
reviewIssues: Translation drifted from the Urdu transcript

title: The Father's Gate to Paradise
summary: In a Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) highlighted the great importance of parents, stating that the father is like the best gate of Paradise.
translation: In the sacred Hadith, parents hold a very high status and position. In one Hadith, the Holy Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'The father is the best of the gates of Paradise, so if you wish, lose that gate or protect it.' This is narrated in Tirmidhi. In this narration of Tirmidhi Sharif, the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) instructed that the father is one of the best gates of Paradise. Thus, if you wish, you may squander this gate or safeguard this gate and this father.

title: Respecting Parents in Islam
summary: The hadith emphasizes that insulting someone else's parents is akin to insulting one's own, as it provokes reciprocal disrespect. This is considered a major sin.
translation: In our conversations today, curses for parents are commonly used. If we curse another person’s parents, it is as if we are cursing our own. It is mentioned in a hadith that disrespecting the parents of others and speaking ill of them is forbidden. Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stated that it is a major sin for a person to curse their own parents. The Companions asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, can a person curse their own parents?' He replied, 'Yes, a person can curse their own parents by cursing someone else's father, causing that person to retaliate by cursing their father, and by cursing someone else's mother, causing that person to curse their mother.' Thus, through this hadith, two things are understood: Firstly, cursing one’s own parents is a major sin. Secondly, if someone curses another's parents and, in turn, that person curses their parents back, it is still considered a major sin. This is because the initial provocation led to the curse of their own parents. Therefore, one must respect others' parents and honor them to ensure mutual respect. Thus, being a cause or reason for sin makes one equally complicit in that sin.

title: Six Forbidden Acts in Islam
summary: The hadith emphasizes six forbidden acts for Muslims, including disrespect to parents, unjust withholding and demanding of wealth, the burial of daughters alive, idle talk, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth. These teachings aim to promote respect, proper financial conduct, and thoughtful communication.
translation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was endowed with Jawami al-Kalim, which means that he spoke few words with profound, comprehensive meaning. One such saying is narrated by Mughira bin Shu'bah (may Allah be pleased with him), where the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden for you disobedience to mothers, withholding what is due and demanding what is not due, and the burial of daughters alive. And He dislikes for you idle talk, persistent questioning, and wasting wealth.' This hadith is found in both Bukhari and Muslim and covers six acts that are forbidden for the Muslim community: disobedience to parents, withholding obligatory due wealth, demanding undeserved wealth, burying daughters alive, engaging in idle talk, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth.
