title: Kindness to Father's Friends
summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) taught that one of the best deeds is to maintain good relations with one's father's friends, especially after the father's passing.
translation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, as reported by Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them), that one of the greatest acts of righteousness is for a person to maintain good relations with the friends of their father. This hadith is narrated by Imam Muslim. It highlights the importance of respecting and honoring one's father and, additionally, his friends, especially after the father has passed away. Being kind to those friends whom the father treated well in life is emphasized.

title: Kindness to Parents After Their Passing
summary: A man from Banu Salma asked the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) if there were any acts of kindness left for him to perform for his deceased parents. The Prophet advised praying and seeking forgiveness for them, fulfilling their promises, maintaining family ties, and honoring their friends. Such actions are recorded as righteousness. It is noted that someone who was disobedient during their parents' lives but commits to these acts after is considered obedient, while the reverse situation deems one disobedient. Therefore, one should honor their parents in life and death as a path to Paradise.
translation: Narrated Abu Usaid Malik bin Rabi'a Sa'idi (RA): We were with the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) when a man from Banu Salma came and asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, is there any act of kindness left that I can do for my parents after they have passed away?' The Prophet (PBUH) replied, 'Yes, praying for them and asking forgiveness for them, fulfilling their vows, maintaining ties with relatives which were dependent on them, and honoring their friends.' These actions, if performed, make a person among the righteous. Imam Suyuti quoted Imam Awza'i, stating that a person who was disobedient during their parents' lives but fulfills these acts after their passing is considered obedient. Conversely, one obedient during their parents' lives but neglectful after their passing is deemed disobedient. Therefore, value parents in their lifetime and after, as it opens the gate to Paradise through their contentment, unlike any other entitlement.

title: Mercy for Young, Respect for Elders
summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized the importance of having mercy on the young and recognizing the honor of elders. A society where people show compassion to children and respect to the elderly fosters peace and harmony. One notable instance is when the Prophet expressed affection for a child, illustrating the value of mercy bestowed by Allah. Respecting elders' dignity is a key Islamic teaching, aligning with the values a true Muslim should follow.
translation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not one of us who does not have mercy on our young ones and does not recognize the honor and dignity of our elders.' This well-known hadith highlights the importance of maintaining respect and compassion in society. By showing mercy to the young and honoring the elders, peace and respect are upheld within the community. For instance, when the Prophet lovingly showed affection to a child, a companion remarked about his own lack of such behavior. The Prophet replied that mercy is a blessing from Allah and emphasized the significant position of elders in Islamic teachings. A true Muslim embodies these values in life.
reviewIssues: Reworded title for practicality

title: Treating People by Their Status
summary: A hadith from Abu Dawood, narrated by Maimoon ibn Abi Shabeeb, describes an incident with Hazrat Aisha (RA) who treated people according to their social status. She gave bread to a beggar but invited a well-dressed man for a meal. When questioned, she explained that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) instructed to treat people according to their rank in society. This teaching emphasizes maintaining societal balance through appropriate recognition and roles.
translation: There is a hadith in Abu Dawood Sharif, narrated by Maimoon ibn Abi Shabeeb, may Allah have mercy on him. He relates that a beggar came to Hazrat Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) and she gave him a piece of bread. Then another man passed by, who was well-dressed and in good condition. She invited him to sit and eat. When asked why, Hazrat Aisha replied, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Assign people to their rightful status." This means to honor people according to their rank. Imam Abu Dawood noted that Maimoon did not meet Hazrat Aisha, but Imam Muslim mentioned this at the beginning of his Sahih as a commentary, stating that Hazrat Aisha shared that the Prophet instructed us to recognize people's ranks. Therefore, this incident teaches us the importance of acknowledging and respecting individual statuses to maintain order. Mulla Ali Qari explains that even angels have specific positions as mentioned in the Quran, reinforcing this hadith. It emphasizes the balance required in assigning responsibilities and highlights the chaos that ensues when roles are given to unsuitable individuals, a reflection of the wise saying that the end times await when tasks are handled by the incompetent. This hadith prompts thoughtful consideration of societal roles and responsibilities.

title: Umar's Anger Calmed by Quranic Guidance
summary: Iyainah bin Hisn criticized Umar ibn al-Khattab for not being generous and fair, which angered Umar. Harb bin Qais reminded Umar of a Quranic verse advising to forgive, promote good, and avoid ignorance. This calmed Umar, highlighting the Sahaba's commitment to Quranic teachings.
translation: Narrated by Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him: Iyainah bin Hisn came and stayed with his nephew, Harb bin Qais, who was part of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him's advisory committee. Iyainah requested his nephew to seek permission for him to meet Umar. Umar granted permission. When Iyainah entered, he said, 'O Ibn Khattab, by Allah, you do not give us generously, nor do you judge fairly between us.' Umar, hearing this, was angered to the point of intending to harm him. Then Harb bin Qais said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, Allah has said to His Prophet, Peace and Blessings be upon him: Take what is given freely, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant. (Quran 7:199) And my uncle is one of the ignorant.' Upon hearing this verse, Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, ceased his anger, as he was very responsive to the Book of Allah. This hadith illustrates the profound impact of the Prophet's companionship and the guidance of the Quran upon the Sahaba, leading them to immediate implementation of its teachings, even amidst anger. The verse is a comprehensive guidance on noble character, advising to accept the goodness in people, guide the wrongdoer with kindness, and avoid engaging in ignorant behavior.

title: Charity and Forgiveness Benefits
summary: The Prophet Muhammad highlighted that giving charity does not reduce wealth and forgiving others increases one's honor.
translation: Abu Huraira (may Allah be pleased with him) reported a hadith: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said three things: Giving charity does not decrease wealth, and whoever forgives a mistake, Allah increases his honor.

title: Warning Relatives about the Fire
summary: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ emphasized personal responsibility for one's deeds and warned his close relatives, including Hazrat Fatimah, to save themselves from Hell. He clarified that family ties would not benefit in the Hereafter unless one has done good deeds.
translation: Today, we consider family ties as a means of worldly honor and reputation; however, these will not benefit us in the Hereafter as much as our own deeds prepared for it will. Thus, when the verse 'And warn your nearest kindred' was revealed, the blessed hadith states: When this verse 'And warn your nearest kindred' was revealed, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ convened the Quraysh. They gathered, and he addressed them generally and specifically by tribe, calling, 'O sons of Abd Shams, O sons of Ka'b bin Lu'ayy, save yourselves from the Fire. O sons of Murrah bin Ka'b, save yourselves from the Fire. O sons of Abd Manaf, save yourselves from the Fire. O sons of Hashim,' and so on, naming them to save themselves from the Fire. Even Hazrat Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her) was present, and he said, 'O Fatimah, save yourself from the Fire, for I possess no power over you from Allah in any manner, except that you have a kinship with me which I will uphold.' He emphasized that his position as a Prophet and the virtuous daughter he was blessed with, and the unique favors granted to him by Allah do not give him power over the affairs of others in the Hereafter. The kinship bond is honored in this world, not in the Hereafter. Therefore, relying solely on familial connections for worldly prestige will not benefit us in the Hereafter. We should engage in deeds to please Allah and continuously accumulate good actions for the Hereafter. May Allah include us among His accepted servants and grant us salvation from Hell.

title: The Example of Good and Bad Companions
summary: The Hadith illustrates the impact of good and bad company. Good companions are likened to a musk carrier who spreads pleasant fragrance, while bad companions are compared to a blacksmith's bellows, which produce an unpleasant odor. This emphasizes the benefits of associating with righteous people and the harms of bad company.
translation: It is important to remember that the company of righteous people leads to goodness for us and our families. By being with good people, we are influenced by their virtues. This is why the Quran orders, 'O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.' Similarly, Hadiths encourage and advise us to join gatherings of good people. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) explained that someone who keeps good company is like a musk carrier, and someone with bad company is like a blacksmith’s bellows. The musk carrier either shares the fragrance with you or you might buy from him, and even if neither, you will at least experience its scent. In contrast, the blacksmith’s bellows either burn your clothes or at least give off an unpleasant smell. Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'The example of a good companion and a bad companion is like the possessor of musk and the one blowing bellows. The possessor of musk will either offer you some, you will buy it, or at least enjoy a good smell from it. The one blowing bellows will either burn your clothes or you will get a foul smell.' Hence, it is explained through examples that associating with good people results in goodness, and with bad people results in harm. As the poet says, when I gain the company of Allah's people, it feels like heaven has descended to earth. Therefore, associating with righteous people brings benefits in this world and the hereafter, while bad company results in losses.

title: Halal Sustenance and Accepted Deeds
summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized that Allah only accepts pure deeds and sustenance. Consuming lawful earnings inspires good actions, while unlawful earnings hinder acceptance of prayers and deeds.
translation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, 'O people, Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure.' He also mentioned that Allah has commanded the believers the same as the messengers: 'O messengers, eat from the good things and do righteous deeds. Surely, I am aware of what you do.' Similarly, 'O you who believe, eat from the good things We have provided for you.' The Prophet described a person traveling, disheveled and dusty, raising his hands in prayer but whose food, drink, clothes, and nourishment are unlawful, questioning how his prayer can be accepted. Lawful sustenance leads to acceptable deeds, whereas unlawful earnings corrupt them, making them unworthy before Allah.

title: Fasting in Shaban Before Ramadan
summary: This hadith discusses the preparation for Ramadan, focusing on the Prophet Muhammad's practice of fasting throughout Shaban. Hazrat Aisha notes that the Prophet never completed a month of fasting except during Ramadan, but he fasted more in Shaban than any other month. Hazrat Umm Salama added that the Prophet fasted consecutively during Shaban and Ramadan, emphasizing preparation without exhausting oneself before Ramadan's obligatory fasts.
translation: As soon as the crescent of Shaban is sighted, a feeling arises in a person's heart that the blessed month of Ramadan is near, prompting preparations for fasting. Allah has shown us an example through the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who would also start preparing for Ramadan in Shaban by fasting abundantly. Hazrat Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "I never saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) complete a month of fasting except in Ramadan, nor did I see him fast more in a month than in Shaban." This hadith is found in Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. Hazrat Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her) reported, "I never saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) fasting for two consecutive months except Shaban and Ramadan," as mentioned in Tirmidhi. The Prophet would fast most of Shaban with minimal breaks to prepare, ensuring nothing hindered the obligatory fasts of Ramadan. One should refrain from excessive fasting in the latter half of Shaban to maintain strength for Ramadan.

title: Teaching Prayer to Children
summary: This hadith stresses the importance of teaching children to pray from an early age. It advises parents to command their children to start praying at seven, and to discipline them by the age of ten if they do not comply. This indicates the significance placed by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) on instilling the habit of prayer from childhood. It also emphasizes teaching religion from a young age as early knowledge is lasting.
translation: Gaining the ability to prostrate before Allah is a great blessing. Our responsibility is not only to be diligent in performing the five daily prayers ourselves but also to ensure our children become regular in prayer and instruct them accordingly. Train and warn them; if they do not comply by the age of ten, they should be disciplined. Pray for them, as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stated: 'Command your children to pray at the age of seven, and if they do not do so by the age of ten, then discipline them.' This shows the emphasis the Prophet placed on instilling the habit of prayer from childhood. It also highlights the importance of teaching religion from a young age, as knowledge acquired in childhood is as enduring as a carving in stone. May Allah grant us correct understanding and the ability to act accordingly.

title: Blessings on the Prophet (PBUH) on Fridays
summary: Encourages Muslims to frequently recite blessings on the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), particularly on Fridays and preceding nights, for greater divine blessings and mercy. Sending even one blessing brings tenfold mercy from Allah, reflecting love and devotion to the Prophet. The Durood Ibrahim is highly recommended, but any words can be used to express these sentiments.
translation: Every Muslim should make it a practice to frequently send blessings (Durood) upon the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on Fridays. There are many virtues of sending blessings, but even greater virtues on Fridays, as narrated by Anas (RA), the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) stated, "Send blessings on me abundantly on Fridays and the night preceding it." Whoever sends one blessing will receive tenfold mercy from Allah. The Quran commands sending blessings upon the Prophet, as in the verse: "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings on him and peace abundantly" (Surah Al-Ahzab, 33:56). When the Companions learned of this verse, they asked for guidance on how to send blessings, and the Prophet taught the Durood Ibrahim, which is recited during prayers. Sending blessings is an obligation at least once in a lifetime, but the more one sends, the better, showcasing faith and love for the Prophet (PBUH). No specific wording is necessary, but the Durood Ibrahim is most recommended. Frequent recitation is encouraged to express love for the Prophet and receive divine mercy. The narration recounts the Prophet smiling upon Angel Gabriel's message that each blessing would result in tenfold mercy. Narrations in Mishkat and Tafsir Qurtubi highlight the rewards for sending blessings. Angels carry the greetings of followers to the Prophet, and those frequent in sending blessings will be closest to him on the Day of Judgment.
reviewIssues: Minor discrepancies in phrase choices regarding mercy and blessings.

title: Importance of Sending Blessings on Friday
summary: The hadith emphasizes the special significance of sending Salawat (blessings) on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) particularly on Fridays. It is mentioned that when a believer sends blessings, Allah sends ten mercies upon them. Studying the Prophet's hadith and sending Salawat as commanded in the Quran is encouraged, with the method of Salawat being taught as Salat al-Ibrahimiyya. Sending frequent Salawat is seen as a sign of love and connection with the Prophet (PBUH) and is expected to result in divine blessings and mercy.
translation: Muslims should frequently send Salawat (blessings) on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on Fridays. It is narrated by Anas (RA) that the Prophet (PBUH) said, 'Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday and Friday night. Whoever sends one Salawat upon me, Allah will send ten mercies upon them.' The Quran commands believers: 'Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, ask [Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [Allah to grant him] peace.' When the companions learned this, they asked about the method of Salawat, and the Prophet taught them Salat al-Ibrahimiyya. Sending Salawat is an obligation at least once in a lifetime. Frequent recitation is considered a sign of faith and love for the Prophet (PBUH). Practicing this brings great mercy to homes and families, with Allah promising multiple blessings for each Salawat. The hadith mentions that those who send Salawat often will be closest to the Prophet (PBUH) on the Day of Judgment, with angels conveying these blessings to him continuously. Therefore, believers should persistently send Salawat to please Allah and the Prophet (PBUH).

title: Importance of Serving Elderly Parents
summary: The hadith emphasizes the importance of serving one's elderly parents. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stressed that failing to gain Paradise through caring for elderly parents makes one deserving of disgrace. Taking care of parents in their old age is a key duty, especially as they become more dependent.
translation: Serving parents is part of a dutiful child's obligation. Allah has decreed that a dutiful child cannot disobey their parents; they must obey unless there is a Shariah contradiction. Otherwise, the child's priority is to honor their parents' instructions. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): 'May his nose be rubbed in dust, may his nose be rubbed in dust, may his nose be rubbed in dust, who finds his parents, one or both, in old age and does not enter Paradise by serving them.' This implies that serving parents is always necessary, especially in old age when they need care and kindness the most. If a person serves their parents in such a state, the parents' heartfelt prayers can make the person deserving of Paradise. The Prophet (peace be upon him) emphasized that if one cannot become deserving of Paradise by serving their elderly parents and receiving their prayers, such a person is worthy of disgrace and being brought low, deserving of no respect.

title: Maintaining Family Ties for Blessings
summary: Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized that maintaining family ties leads to blessings in sustenance and longevity.
translation: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'If you desire blessings in your sustenance and a long life, you must do one thing. If a person performs it, Allah will grant them both blessings. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, whoever wants abundance and blessings in their sustenance and a long life should maintain family ties, fulfill the rights of relatives, and recognize these as responsibilities. Ensure that these ties are upheld, not letting them end with the passing of a relative. Continue to maintain each relationship according to its rights, and as a result, blessings and longevity will be granted.'

title: Prioritizing Service to Parents
summary: Serving living parents is highly emphasized, taking precedence over non-obligatory acts, even striving in Allah's path.
translation: If parents are alive, a man's greatest blessing is to always be available for their service and promptly respond to their every call. This is essential because such an opportunity exists only while they are living. Once they pass away, no amount of good deeds can truly replace this, not even striving in the path of Allah. A hadith reported by Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with them) illustrates this: A man came to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and expressed his desire to pledge for migration and striving for reward from Allah. The Prophet (peace be upon him) asked if his parents were alive. He replied that both his father and mother were alive. The Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed that if he sought reward from Allah, he should return to his parents and treat them well. This indicates that serving one's parents should be prioritized over other non-obligatory acts if it leads to divine reward, unless fulfilling obligatory duties requires otherwise.

title: Positive Assumptions About Allah at Death
summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) instructed that one should face death with good assumptions about Allah. This hadith, recorded in Sahih Muslim, was conveyed three days before his passing. It emphasizes avoiding negative thoughts about Allah during difficult times and maintaining engagement in good deeds. It is believed that individuals will be resurrected based on their state and intentions at the time of death.
translation: Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'None of you should die except while assuming good about Allah.' This hadith, narrated by Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) and recorded in Sahih Muslim, advises believers to avoid negative assumptions about Allah, especially during tough situations. Good deeds should be maintained, as one’s state at death will be their state at resurrection. 'Every servant will be resurrected upon what they died doing.'

title: Repentance and Divine Mercy
summary: Cry out of fear of Allah for His mercy and protection from Hellfire.
translation: Tonight is the night of Jumu'ah. You all are aware of the situation in Turkey, which partly involves our sins, causing distress to our brothers there. Therefore, especially make supplications for them, for yourselves, and for forgiveness of sins. When we pray, our supplications will have an effect. Especially today, we recognize our own sins and Allah is aware of them. We should cry and beseech before Allah. Allah loves this weeping. In a sacred Hadith, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'The person who cries due to the fear of Allah will not enter Hell until the milk returns to the udder.' This means that once milk is taken out, it cannot return, similar to the Quran's mention—that a camel will not pass through the eye of a needle. Just as a camel cannot pass through the needle’s eye, extracted milk cannot return to the udder. Likewise, a sinful person who cries out of fear of Allah will never enter Hell and will not be cast into the Fire.
reviewIssues: Title was not suitable: Changed to reflect the content more accurately.
Translation required minor adjustments for clarity and retention of meaning.

title: Accepting Gifts in Islam
summary: This hadith discusses the importance of accepting gifts with sincerity, considering the intention behind the gift, and ensuring it is acquired through lawful means. It highlights the teachings of Imam Al-Ghazali and the practices of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his Companions, particularly focusing on the behavior of Abdullah bin Umar.
translation: A common observation is that people often refuse gifts. Even if someone is prosperous, giving and receiving gifts are both Sunnah. One should accept a gift even if they are well off. Often, personal pride hinders acceptance. Imam Al-Ghazali states that when accepting a gift, consider the giver’s intention: is it for charity, affection, fame, or bribery? A true gift is sincere with no hidden intentions. Also, consider the recipient's intention; if driven by greed, it should not be accepted. However, if received without greed and as a provision from Allah, it should be accepted, provided the wealth is halal, not haram. This behavior is evidenced in the lives of the Companions and followers, who accepted some gifts and rejected others. There’s a hadith narrated by Salim from his father Abdullah bin Umar (may Allah be pleased with them) that when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) would give Abdullah a gift, he would suggest giving it to someone more in need. The Prophet insisted on acceptance, saying if wealth is offered without desire or request, accept it, incorporate it into your wealth, then choose to use or donate it. Salim mentions that Abdullah bin Umar never asked for anything but also did not refuse unsolicited gifts, influenced by the Prophet’s teachings.

title: Virtue of Earning Through Honest Labor
summary: This hadith highlights the virtue of earning a living through one's own efforts rather than relying on others. It mentions that relying on others can signify weakness, which is discouraged in Islam. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized that it is better to work for oneself, even if it means gathering and selling firewood, than to ask others for help. The hadith also discusses the different rulings on earning depending on intentions and needs.
translation: In earning, a person who earns his livelihood through his own labor and then feeds himself and his family holds great virtue. Islam has always encouraged this practice, indicating that relying on someone else's mercy or hope signifies weakness, which Islam disapproves of. Thus, many encouragements are mentioned in the noble Hadith. Listen to one Hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who says, 'One of you carries a bundle of wood on his back and then sells it, and this is better for him than asking someone who might give or not give.' Therefore, scholars say that earning is sometimes obligatory, sometimes forbidden, sometimes recommended, and sometimes permissible. It is obligatory when it meets the necessary needs of the earner and their family. It is forbidden when earned for pride and ostentation. It is recommended when one earns more than the need with the intention of giving the surplus to the poor, needy, and relatives. It is permissible when one earns more than necessary to maintain one's dignity and status while staying within the bounds of Sharia. It is mentioned about Prophet David (peace be upon him) that he used to eat from his hand's labor. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that Prophet David (peace be upon him) would consume only from his own labor.

title: Shab-e-Barat: Optional Practices
summary: The discussion clarifies that practices on Shab-e-Barat, such as fasting and specific worship, are not obligatory. Personal discretion should be exercised, and while some hadiths discuss the night's virtues, they are weak. Therefore, engaging in these practices is permissible but not mandated. Observing them is rewarded but omitting them is not sinful. People should avoid turning these practices into obligatory activities or organizing large gatherings, such as cemetery visits.
translation:
Regarding Shab-e-Barat, many people are confused by various videos, audios, and speeches, questioning what actions are required and what the ruling is. It should be understood that worship or fasting on this night are not obligatory or necessary acts, such that omission would lead to blame or questioning. It is incorrect to insist on others' fasting or staying awake, as these practices are obligatory only when explicitly commanded by religion.

Regular acts like daily Tahajjud or Quran recitation can be emphasized on this night. Fasting on the 13th, 14th, and 15th days of the lunar month is a habit for some, and Shab-e-Barat fits in naturally with its merits mentioned in hadiths. Although the narrations are weak, several weak hadiths on a subject can raise it to a level of practice.

Some assert there are no authentic hadiths on Shab-e-Barat, and it's valid for those who prefer to not observe it. There shouldn't be conflict over this; it's a personal choice whether to observe it based on individual perspective. Large gatherings or cemetery visits organized with friends are incorrect practices. Individual prayers and remembrances at home are positive.

Fasting, if regularly done on 13th, 14th, and 15th, naturally includes the 15th. Practicing as one's conscience allows is acceptable, as it is not obligatory, leading to no blame whether observed or not. Hence, such acts are discretionary, rewarding those who do and not sinful for those who don’t. However, considering them obligatory can invalidate worship and change the nature of religious intent.

title: Five Nights for Acceptable Prayers
summary: Imam Shafi emphasized five nights when prayers are accepted: the nights before the two Eids, the night of Rajab, the night of Shab-e-Barat, and Friday night, which recurs weekly. Additionally, the fifteenth of Sha'ban is highlighted as important for seeking forgiveness and success.
translation: The respected scholars have written about keeping blessed nights alive through worship and striving to please Allah by staying awake. Imam Shafi, may Allah have mercy on him, referenced in the established Sunnah noted by Sheikh Abdul Haq Muhaddith Dehlvi, mentions five nights during which prayers are accepted. These include the nights before the two Eids (the night before the Eid after Ramadan and the night before Eid al-Adha), the night of Rajab, the night of Shab-e-Barat, and the night of Friday. These are nights during which Allah does not reject prayers. The night of Friday is a recurring blessing every week. Additionally, scholars recommend worship on other blessed nights, such as the fifteenth of Sha'ban, known as Laylat al-Nisf min Sha'ban, highlighting the importance of seeking forgiveness, repenting, and earnestly asking for success in life, ease in the Hereafter, and salvation from Hellfire for oneself, family, and the entire Muslim community.

title: Virtues of Spending in Allah's Path
summary: Spending in the way of Allah is highly virtuous as taught by the Quran and Hadith. The Quran assures that any good done is fully known by Allah and will be rewarded. A noble hadith mentions two people who can be envied in the positive sense: one who uses wealth righteously and one endowed with wisdom who teaches it.
translation: In the Holy Quran and blessed Hadiths, the virtue of spending in the way of Allah is immensely emphasized. The Quran encourages by stating that whatever a person does is in the knowledge of Allah, meaning that Allah will certainly reward and bless you for it. "Whatever good you do, Allah knows it," and in another place, "Whatever you spend of good is for yourself, and whatever you spend, seek only Allah's face, and whatever you spend will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged." Similarly, in a noble hadith narrated by Abdullah bin Masood (may Allah be pleased with him), it is said that there are two types of people who can be envied for the blessings Allah has given them. In Islam, envy is generally prohibited. Envy means wishing for the removal of someone else's blessing and hoping it is bestowed upon oneself. However, scholars interpret envy here as 'Ghibtah', which means desiring a similar blessing without wishing for its removal from the other person. Thus, 'no envy except in two cases': one, a man whom Allah has given wealth, which he uses in a rightful way, and two, a man whom Allah has endowed with wisdom which he uses for judgment and teaches to others. Therefore, one can legitimately aspire to these two qualities alone.

title: Rewards of Quran Recitation Effort
summary: Even those who struggle while reciting the Quran are promised double the reward, emphasizing its importance in a Muslim's life.
translation: Incorporate the recitation of the Holy Quran into our routines such that it becomes indispensable in our lives. This should define a Muslim. The Hadith leaves no excuse for someone claiming inability to read the Quran. The Hadith promises double reward for a person who struggles to recite properly. According to a Hadith narrated by Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (may Allah be pleased with her), the Prophet (peace be upon him) said that a person who reads the Quran expertly will be among the noble, righteous angels on the Day of Judgment. However, a person who reads with difficulty and effort will receive double reward: one for the recitation and another for the effort put into it.

title: Nearness to Allah and Divine Forgiveness
summary: This hadith emphasizes Allah's immense mercy and readiness to forgive those who sincerely turn towards Him. It describes how Allah draws even closer to those who make an effort to approach Him, by forgiving sins and offering rewards for good deeds many times over, provided that people maintain faith in His oneness.
translation: The month of Ramadan is very near. We should turn to Allah and attach ourselves to Him. When a servant draws near to Allah by a span, Allah comes closer by a hand-span, and if someone comes closer by a hand-span, Allah comes closer by two hands. The hadith narrated from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) mentions that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said that Allah, the Exalted, says: Whoever does a good deed will have a tenfold reward or even more; and whoever does an evil deed, he will be recompensed only equivalent to it, or I may forgive him. Whoever comes near Me by a span, I will come nearer by a hand-span; whoever comes near Me by a hand-span, I will come nearer by the arm’s length; whoever comes walking, I will come running to him. Whoever meets Me with sins as large as the earth, not associating anything with Me, I will meet him with forgiveness equivalent to his sins. This is a special blessing for the followers of the Prophet (peace be upon him), highlighting Allah's kindness and His boundless forgiveness, ready to embrace anyone who sincerely turns to Him.

title: Major Sins: False Oaths
summary: Taking false oaths is among the major sins in Islam, as highlighted in a hadith by the Prophet (peace be upon him). These sins include associating partners with Allah, disobeying parents, taking a life unjustly, and committing perjury. The term 'Yameen Ghamus' is used for a deliberately false oath, which leads one into sin. Three types of oaths are discussed: 'Yameen Laghw,' a mistaken false oath about the past, 'Yameen Mun'aqidah,' an oath about future actions requiring expiation if broken, and 'Yameen Ghamus,' a deliberate false oath about the past, with differing scholarly opinions regarding expiation 'Yameen Ghamus.'
translation: Taking a false oath is considered one of the major sins. In a hadith, several major sins are mentioned by the Prophet (peace be upon him): associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, unjustly killing someone, and lying under oath. The term 'غَمُوس' (Ghamus) is used for a deliberate false oath, because it immerses one into sin. 'Ghamus' means 'to drown,' reflecting how the person is submerged in sin. There are three types of oaths: 1) 'Yameen Laghw' - a mistaken false oath about the past, believed to be true, with no sin or expiation according to Imam Abu Hanifa, 2) 'Yameen Mun'aqidah' - an oath about future actions, with expiation needed if broken, 3) 'Yameen Ghamus' - a deliberate false oath about past events, with debate among scholars like Imam Shafi and Imam Abu Hanifa about expiation. Thus, false oaths are major sins in Islamic law, and one should speak truthfully without resorting to oaths.

title: Prophetic Preparation for Ramadan
summary: The Prophet ﷺ would begin preparations for Ramadan in the month of Sha'ban, being particularly attentive to counting its days. Aisha رضي الله عنها noted that this was the month he focused on most for counting days. Upon seeing the Ramadan moon, he would fast; if not, he'd complete thirty days of Sha'ban and then begin fasting.
translation: There are only a few days left for the arrival of Ramadan. It is mentioned about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that He would begin preparation for Ramadan even before its arrival, particularly by spending the month of Sha'ban in anticipation of Ramadan. Umm al-Mu'minin Aisha Siddiqa رضي الله عنها states that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more attentive to counting the days of Sha'ban than any other month. Then, He would fast upon sighting the Ramadan moon. If the sky was cloudy, meaning the crescent was not visible, He would complete thirty days and then commence Ramadan fasting from the first day. This is a hadith from Abu Dawood and Mishkat Sharif. Aisha Siddiqa رضي الله عنها mentions that the Prophet was particular about counting the days of Sha'ban more than any other month. Once the moon of Ramadan was sighted, He would start fasting, and if not sighted due to cloudiness, He would complete the thirty-day count and then start fasting the days of Ramadan from the first date.

title: Unique Blessings of Ramadan
summary: The hadith details five unique blessings granted to the Prophet Muhammad's community during Ramadan, blessings not bestowed on any other community. These include the pleasing smell of a fasting person's mouth to Allah, the sea creatures seeking forgiveness for them, paradise being adorned for their arrival, rebellious devils being locked up, and forgiveness granted on the last night of Ramadan.
translation: Narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that my community has been granted five unique distinctions in the blessed Ramadan that were not given to any other community. Firstly, the smell from the mouth of a fasting person is more beloved to Allah than musk. Secondly, during this time, the fish in the sea seek forgiveness for them until they break their fast. Thirdly, Allah adorns His paradise every day and then says, 'Soon My righteous servants will cast off their hardships and come to you.' Fourthly, the rebellious devils are locked up during Ramadan, so they cannot reach the evils they would during other times. Fifthly, on the last night of Ramadan, their forgiveness is granted. It was asked if this forgiveness was granted on the Night of Decree, to which he replied, 'No, but the common practice is that the laborer is fully paid upon completing their task.'

title: Acceptance of Supplication While Fasting
summary: The hadith emphasizes that the supplications of three individuals are never rejected: the fasting person at iftar, a just ruler, and an oppressed person. The fasting person receives forgiveness prayers from angels and sea creatures. It encourages prayers for personal and communal wellbeing.
translation: The connection between fasting and supplication is profound. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, 'Three people's supplications are not rejected: the fasting person at the time of breaking the fast, the just ruler, and the oppressed person.' This hadith promises that the supplication of a fasting person at iftar will not be rejected. Additionally, a fasting person is honored with forgiveness prayers from angels and sea fish. Therefore, during these blessed moments, one should pray for personal forgiveness, and also remember the entire Muslim Ummah, praying for the alleviation of their sorrows and the restoration of their dignity and happiness. May Allah accept all our supplications.

title: Intercession of Fasting and Quran
summary: The hadith states that on the Day of Judgment, fasting and the Quran will intercede on behalf of the believers. Fasting will say that it kept the person away from food and desires during the day, while the Quran will say that it prevented him from sleeping at night. Both intercessions will be accepted by Allah. This underscores the importance of reciting the Quran, especially during Ramadan, and maintaining devotional practices such as Tarawih prayer.
translation: Fasting is such an act of worship that in the Hereafter, it will intercede for the one who observed it in the presence of Allah, and its intercession will be accepted. Similarly, the Holy Quran will intercede for those who recite it, and this intercession will also be accepted. The Noble Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Fasting and the Quran will intercede for the servant. Fasting will say: O Lord, I kept him from food and desires during the day, so accept my intercession for him. And the Quran will say: I kept him from sleep at night, so accept my intercession for him. Hence, both intercessions will be accepted.' This hadith indicates the importance of reciting the Quran, especially in Ramadan, and emphasizes listening to the Quran in Tarawih and maintaining the nightly prayers throughout the entire month.
